what: Tower Semiconductor is a foundry: it makes chips designed by other companies. It specialises not in the smallest transistors but in analogue chips, radio-frequency parts, image sensors and silicon photonics.
customers: Chip designers in automotive, medical, industrial and communications markets who do not own a factory.
money: chips for phones, satellites and data centre optics
moat: Specialised process recipes built over decades for analogue chips, which cannot simply be moved to another foundry: a customer requalifying a design elsewhere faces a year of work.
risks: 41 times earnings for a business whose revenue is still below its 2022 level
Factories in Israel, which carries geopolitical risk that competitors do not share
Foundry capacity is capital-hungry: staying current means spending heavily every year
opportunities: Analysts see about 115% upside, the widest gap on this list, with 10 covering the stock
Silicon photonics is the technology data centres use to move light between chips, and demand has turned up with AI build-outs
$1.2B of cash against $178M of debt, so the next capacity expansion can be self-funded
watch: Capacity utilisation and whether the silicon photonics orders turn into revenue.
